content.content:
Fred,

I'm in LA from tomorrow for Dentsu and the Griffin AGM, so can you take over the vendor and partner backlog this week? That's anyone outside the investor work who has an offer, a trial, a quote, terms or an ask in front of us and that one of us has actually engaged with: a call, a reply, a sign-up or paper. Cold pitches nobody answered, including ones we only forwarded around internally, stay off it, and so do the ad networks, PlayableX, Craftsman+ and Singular (they all stay on the UA budget call), the investors, and Mattel, which I'm keeping.

Go by the runway guardrails doc for what we do with each one, plus the one change I posted in #executives on Monday. Anything that needs signing goes the way ESG's note about signing says.

Everyone who is waiting to hear from us should get a written answer this week. Get each company's contact into Contacts so we're not digging through mail next time.

Log it all in a sheet in the Q4 commitments folder, the README in the folder has the columns. Then reply here with what we're keeping and what's waiting on Arthur or me to sign.

Thanks,
Leonard

{"documentId": "f_b98287f6f80fe431a71209", "title": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "name": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "revisionId": "0d3b4ff7c7", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T16:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "text": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments
Leonard, Sep 26. Until we know where the raise lands, this is how we handle anything outside the investor work that wants money, a signature or an answer from us.
How to decide
Go top to bottom and stop at the first one that fits.
1. Already answered. If one of us has already given them an answer, don't write to them again. Note who answered and when. If the answer was "later", it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars too.
2. Cash test. Anything that would cost us cash between Oct 1 and Dec 31 ends now: say no, or cancel it in writing the way their paper or notice asks. A trial or pilot that turns into a paid plan inside that window counts as cash, and so does an offer we would have to take up and pay for before January. Travel and event costs count only when we book them ourselves.
3. Keep. The cash test has one exception: anything on Arthur's keep-running list on our board stays, even if it costs money. Tell them we're staying.
4. Sign. If it costs nothing before January but taking it means someone has to accept terms or sign for the company, it goes the way ESG's note says. Tell them it's with Leonard or Arthur to sign, and with our lawyers first when ESG has to see it.
5. Park. Everything else that's free until January, including offers we could still take up after that. Tell them we'll pick it up in January; it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars (first week of January).
Answers
Everyone who is waiting to hear from us gets a written answer. Portals and no-reply notices don't need one.
"}

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

1759288987.503349 2025-10-01T03:23:07Z Leonard Hayes : We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it’s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,
[PERSON_NAME_9449], on behalf of the Speedrun team | replies None

content.content:
Hi Leonard,

Following up on our call today, here's how we'd like agreements handled from now on while you're raising:

- Only an officer, you or Arthur, accepts terms or signs for Harmony Games, whatever the amount. That includes click-through terms and portal NDAs.
- Anything with an automatic renewal, exclusivity, a licence of your IP or a term over 12 months comes to us before anyone signs. Send each one to our intake address (it's in your Contacts as ESG Law intake), one email per agreement, so we can open a matter for it.
- Mutual NDAs on our template don't need review, whatever their term. An officer can sign them.

Best,
PERSON_2694_NAME
PARTNER, ESG Law
====
Agreed. This replaces what I said in July about Fred signing small stuff himself.

Fred, Arthur: anything waiting on Arthur or me to sign, put it on our founders' board To Do list with the company's name in the card title, including the ones that go to ESG. For the intake emails, what to include is in the intake checklist I shared.

Leonard
====

content.content:
Hi Frederick,

Heads-up that the free Starter tier on your account ends on Oct 31. From Nov 1 the account moves to Team ($29/month) under your existing agreement, so phone and SMS paging keep working for your on-call rota. If you'd rather drop back to the free plan, reply and I'll downgrade you before then. Free has email alerts only, no paging.

Can you confirm either way?

Dana Whitfield
Customer Success, Pingwise
---
Hi Frederick,

Quick one: we're retiring the old Starter tier, so your nightly database backups move to Standard ($19/month) when the plan renews on Oct 12. Can you confirm you want to keep them running? If not, I'll stop the backups at renewal.

Mila
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for the call on Tuesday. As promised, the order form for Pro is attached: 4 seats, unlimited template and stock-clip downloads. Pro starts Nov 1 at $149/month, billed monthly, and you keep the free seat until then.

Can you let me know by mid-October if we should set it up?

Best,
Maren
---
Hi Frederick,

Great chatting. Proposal attached for a pre-registration push at the Seattle Indie Expo on Nov 7: we cover the stand and two passes, you cover travel for two. We'll book the flights and hotel and invoice you at cost.

Sven
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for the chat. I've sent our deck for the holiday puzzle bundle: no cost to join, and it includes a licence to use Domino Delights' name and art in the bundle marketing. Submissions close Nov 1.

Freya
---
Hi Frederick,

Following our call, the letter of intent is attached: we'd publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea on a revenue share, at no cost to you. It includes 12 months' exclusivity for those markets while we prepare the launch. We'd need it signed by Oct 20.

Noor
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for applying to the Lumencloud Startup Program. Good news, Harmony Games qualifies for $25,000 in Lumencloud credits. The program agreement is attached; it's a 36-month term and the credits start once it's signed. Applications for this cohort close Oct 31.

Aiden
---
Hi Frederick,

Good to talk yesterday. Here's the launch package for your 2026 release: newswire distribution plus 40 targeted outlets, $1,200 when you book. No travel, all remote, and you can book any time before launch. Let me know if you'd like to go ahead.

Ava
---
Hi Frederick,

Following up on our chat, we've reserved $10,000 of Cloudlark credits for Harmony Games and will hold them until Feb 28. Nothing to do until you want to activate them. Would you like to activate now or later?

Yara
---
Hi Frederick,

Following our call, here's the proposal for a November creator campaign with 8 mid-tier TikTok and YouTube creators. We take a 50% deposit when you book, and bookings close Oct 31 for the November slots.

Kofi
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for the call on Wednesday. We'd like to feature Zombie Match 3D in our November puzzle week. The featuring agreement has to be accepted in our partner portal by an authorised signatory of the company. No fees. Could that happen by Oct 24?

Mateo
---
Hi Frederick,

As discussed, the free tier covers alerts for 'Zombie Match 3D' and 'Harmony Games' on the app stores and socials. To switch it on, accept the terms in the dashboard and you're set. Nothing to pay.

Leah
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for taking my call last week. I've sent over our proposal deck for publishing Domino Delights in Southeast Asia: we handle localization, store featuring and UA in the region on a revenue share, no upfront fee. Happy to walk your team through it.

Wen Halvorsen
Partnerships, Lanternfly Publishing
---

values: Creative retainer proposal: $3,500/month from Oct 1, 3-month minimum; asked us to confirm by Oct 1
Not going ahead with the retainer; please don't book the team for October
ASO retainer proposal: $900/month from Oct 1 (3-month start); asked us to confirm by Oct 1
Not going ahead with the ASO retainer; no contract needed
Store listing localization quote: $2,640 for 12 languages, invoiced on delivery; quote valid until Oct 3; waiting on a PO
Not placing the PO; passing on the localization quote
Moderated player panel order form: $1,200 prepaid, panel Oct 14; confirm by Oct 6
Not confirming the Oct 14 panel; please don't recruit
Bay Area Indie Showcase booth hold (Oct 24): $4,800, $2,400 deposit due Oct 10 (Fred's June reply only said he'd come back)
Releasing the booth hold; we won't pay the deposit
Trailer music pack annual licence: $1,188 paid on signature; quote valid until Oct 15
Passing on the trailer music licence; no need to send it for signature
UGC Studio pilot (HG-2291) hit its 20-video cap; pilot ends Oct 15 and Studio plan starts Oct 16 at $1,800/month unless cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io by Oct 15
Cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io (per the Paylane notice) and told Priya we're not continuing after the pilot
Pro order form: 4 seats, $149/month billed from Nov 1; asked for an answer by mid-October
Not taking Pro; please don't set it up
Seattle Indie Expo pre-registration push (Nov 7): we'd pay travel/hotel for two (~$1,600) that Wishwave books and invoices; confirm by Oct 17
Not going ahead; please don't book travel (partner-booked travel counts as cash)
30-day trial from Sep 19 converts to Growth at $79/month on Oct 20 unless cancelled by Oct 19; offered a walkthrough
Cancel the trial before it converts; no walkthrough needed
November creator campaign: $8,000 budget, 50% deposit on booking; book by Oct 31
Nightly DB backups move to Standard at $19/month at the Oct 12 renewal; asked us to confirm
We're staying on Standard; keep the nightly backups running (on Arthur's keep-running list)
SSL cert for the game API domain expires Oct 20; renewal $89/year; reply to confirm
Please renew and reissue the API domain certificate; we're staying (on Arthur's keep-running list)
Night pager / on-call paging: free Starter ends Oct 31, moves to Team at $29/month from Nov 1 under existing agreement
We're staying on Team; keep phone/SMS paging, don't downgrade (on Arthur's keep-running list)
Publishing LOI for Zombie Match 3D in Japan/Korea: revenue share, no fees, 12 months' exclusivity; signature needed by Oct 20
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign
Mutual NDA on ESG's template (2-year term) before the Oct 8 call
It's with Leonard or Arthur to sign; on our template, so no lawyer review needed
November puzzle week featuring agreement: no fees, promotion-only term; must be accepted in the partner portal by an authorised signatory by Oct 24
It's with Leonard or Arthur to accept in the portal
Startup Program: $25k credits, 36-month agreement, no charges while credits last; sign by Oct 31 (cohort closes)
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign
Holiday puzzle bundle for Domino Delights: no cost, rev share; participation agreement licenses our name/logo/art for 18 months; sign by Nov 1
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign
Southeast Asia publishing proposal for Domino Delights: 70/30 rev share, no upfront fee, 2-year exclusive term (Fred's Sep 10 reply only said we'd get back)
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign
Free brand-monitoring tier; activation means accepting click-through terms in the dashboard
Keep the setup on hold; Leonard or Arthur will accept the terms
Quote for 12 rigged monster models: $6,400, 50% on kickoff
Arthur passed: keeping the art in-house (no further reply sent)
Font app-embedding licence quote: $640 payable on order; valid until Jan 31, 2026
We'll pick it up in January
Beta free through Jan 31, 2026, paid plans from February; asked for a feedback call
We'll pick it up in January
Team trial free until Feb 1, 2026, then $8/user/month; offered to add the rest of the team
We'll pick it up in January; no need to add more users now
Trailer voice-over quote: $950 paid on booking; valid until Feb 28, 2026
We'll pick it up in January
Free sample report sent; full set is $300/month from February 2026 if we subscribe
Thanks for the sample; we'll pick it up in January
Free pilot slot in February 2026 for the website demo widget; asked whether to hold it
We'll pick it up in January
Pro upgrade proposal ($49/month from upgrade); free plan continues
Staying on the free plan; we'll pick it up in January
Startup trial free until Jan 12, 2026, then Growth $99/month unless cancelled; asked if we'll stay on
We'll pick it up in January (before the trial ends)
$10k credits reserved until Feb 28, 2026; activate now or later?
Later; we'll pick it up in January
Launch package for 2026 release: $1,200 paid when booked, book any time before launch
We'll pick it up in January
Social scheduler: startup promo free until Jan 31, 2026, then $39/month unless cancelled; asked if we'll keep it
We'll pick it up in January

input.body:
Hi ESG team,

Please open a matter for this one.

- Company and agreement: Kinetic Arcade, letter of intent to publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea
- Term and automatic renewal: 12 months from signature; no automatic renewal stated
- Exclusivity / licence of our IP: yes, 12 months' exclusivity for Japan and Korea
- Cost to us: none (revenue share, no fees to Harmony Games)
- Needed by: Oct 20, 2025
- Who would sign: Leonard Hayes or Arthur Blake

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.subject: Cancellation - workspace HG-2291 (UGC Studio) - Harmony Games
input.body:
Hello,

Harmony Games is cancelling the UGC Studio plan on workspace HG-2291, effective at the end of the pilot on Oct 15, 2025. Please do not start the Studio plan on Oct 16 or bill us for it.

Please confirm the cancellation in writing.

Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.body:
Leonard,

Done. 33 companies are logged in "Q4 commitments log" in the Q4 commitments folder: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/3f148431673609df/edit
Everyone who was waiting has a written answer, and each contact is now in Contacts.

KEEPING (Arthur's keep-running list):
- Vaultline: nightly DB backups, $19/month from the Oct 12 renewal
- Certwell: API domain SSL cert, $89/year, renews before it lapses Oct 20
- Pingwise: night pager, $29/month on Team from Nov 1 (told them not to downgrade)
None of the three needs a new signature.

WAITING ON YOU OR ARTHUR TO SIGN (cards are on the Harmony Games board To Do list):
With ESG first (intake email sent for each one):
- Kinetic Arcade: Japan/Korea publishing LOI with 12 months' exclusivity. Sign by Oct 20
- Lumencloud: $25k credits, 36-month agreement. Sign by Oct 31
- Bundlehouse: holiday bundle; the agreement licenses Domino Delights' name and art for 18 months. Sign by Nov 1
- Lanternfly: SEA publishing for Domino Delights, 2-year exclusive. No date given
No ESG review needed:
- Playfuse: mutual NDA on ESG's template. Before the Oct 8 call
- Orbit Store: November featuring agreement, accepted in their portal. By Oct 24
- Markward: click-through terms for the free brand-monitoring tier. No date

Everything else:
- Ended (cash before January), 11: Brightlane, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor (Bay Area booth deposit), Soundvault, Framewell, Wishwave (partner-booked travel counts as cash, per your Monday change), Streamcast, plus Reviewly and Clipforge. Those last two were trials that turn paid on Oct 20 and Oct 16. Clipforge's cancellation went to billing@paylane.io in writing, as their notice requires.
- Parked for the Jan 5 review, 11: Glyphworks, Quillcraft, Loopnote, Driftwood Audio, Benchmarkly, Tilecast, Echohall, Retainly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam, Hootline. Each has a reminder on my calendar for Jan 5.
- Already answered: Motive Forge. Arthur passed on Sep 19, so I didn't write to them again.
- Left off the list: Spotlight Fest and Nova Rewards were cold pitches nobody answered, and Nova has since withdrawn.

Fred

content.text:
I've worked through the whole backlog using Leonard's runway guardrails, his Monday change, and ESG's note on signing. Every company that was waiting on us now has a written answer, and I've replied to Leonard on his email with what we're keeping and what's waiting on him or Arthur to sign.

**The log** is a new sheet, "Q4 commitments log", in your Q4 commitments folder, set up from Leonard's template and shared with him. It has one row per company, 33 in all:

| Decision | Count | Companies |
|---|---|---|
| End (would cost cash before January) | 11 | Brightlane Studio, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor Events, Soundvault, Framewell, Wishwave, Streamcast Talent, Reviewly, Clipforge |
| Keep (on Arthur's keep-running list) | 3 | Vaultline, Certwell, Pingwise (Pingwise is the night pager on his list) |
| Sign | 7 | Kinetic Arcade, Lumencloud, Bundlehouse, Lanternfly, Playfuse, Orbit Store, Markward |
| Park until January | 11 | Glyphworks, Quillcraft, Loopnote, Driftwood Audio, Benchmarkly, Tilecast, Echohall, Retainly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam, Hootline |
| Already answered | 1 | Motive Forge (Arthur passed on Sep 19, so I didn't write to them again) |

**Calls you might want to double-check:**
- **Reviewly and Clipforge are ended, not parked.** Each trial turns into a paid plan inside October: Reviewly at $79/month on Oct 20, Clipforge at $1,800/month on Oct 16. I asked Hana at Reviewly to cancel, and sent Clipforge's cancellation to billing@paylane.io, as their notice requires.
- **Wishwave is ended.** Its Seattle expo offer has them booking our travel and billing us about $1,600, which counts as cash under Leonard's Monday change.
- **Pixel Harbor and Lanternfly weren't treated as answered.** Your earlier replies only said you'd come back to them, so I didn't count those as answers.
- **Lanternfly goes to the lawyers.** Their deck shows a 2-year exclusive deal, which needs ESG review before anyone signs.
- **Spotlight Fest and Nova Rewards are left off.** Both were cold pitches nobody answered, and Nova has since withdrawn.

**Signing:** the seven Sign companies each have a card on the Harmony Games board's To Do list, with deadlines where the company gave one. Four of them go to ESG first, and I sent one intake email per agreement: Kinetic Arcade (by Oct 20), Lumencloud (Oct 31), Bundlehouse (Nov 1) and Lanternfly (no date). The other three Leonard or Arthur can sign directly: Playfuse's NDA (before the Oct 8 call), Orbit Store's portal agreement (Oct 24) and Markward's click-through terms.

**January:** Leonard's review is Monday, Jan 5, 2026. Your calendar has 11 all-day reminders that day, one for each parked company.

**Contacts:** I added 30 vendor contacts with their company in the job field. Leah (Markward), Aiden (Lumencloud) and Noor (Kinetic Arcade) were already there.

**Coming up soon:** Brightlane and Ascendo wanted an answer today, and both got their no. Next is Lingora's quote, which expires Oct 3; they've already had their answer too.
